system_note: The one code system membership is tested in. Synthea codes MedicationRequest at clinical-drug level -- 310798, 314076, 105585 -- and a knowledge-table row declares an ingredient, so a row's ingredient code compared against a prescription's code matches nothing in any of the fourteen committed bundles: measured, zero hits. That is REQ-59's failure one layer up, and this file is what closes it (REQ-63, D119).
compiled_from: One record per ingredient a row of medication_effects.json declares, expanded to every RxNorm concept RxNav relates to that ingredient at IN, SCD and SBD. Multi-ingredient products are included and that is deliberate: a patient on hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG / lisinopril 20 MG Oral Tablet is on both drugs, and both rows should fire.

expansion.source: RxNav, U.S. National Library of Medicine
expansion.note: Pinned, not regenerated by any gate. RxNorm publishes monthly, so a re-expansion is a new compilation adopted deliberately and never as a refresh (D73's shape). Measured at compilation: all five ingredients resolve, the five responses run 1.5-33 KB, a repeat fetch returns byte-identical bytes, and every clinical-drug code the committed bundles prescribe is admitted by its own ingredient's set. The ingredient rxcui itself comes from each row's declared ingredient.source, not from this query.

known_limit: Two of the five ingredients are prescribed nowhere in this corpus -- prednisone and apixaban -- so their expansions are carried and unexercised. They are compiled anyway: the table declares five rows and a matcher that covers three of them would answer for the other two by omission, which is the silent-skip this project refuses elsewhere (REQ-57's shape). Suppression and colouring are the engine's; this file only answers whether a prescription is the drug.
